transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom / Fireflies recording
Attendees: Lila Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Rivera (Redwood SE), Jin Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (Apollo CTO), Samir Patel (Apollo Head Infra), Meghan O'Connor (PM), Eric Zhao (ML Eng)

AUTO-SUMMARY (audio notes): cover capacity sizing for POC, define reserved vs burst strategy, fallback/degarde behavior, run benchmark with 100k tokens.

00:00 - Speaker 1 (Lila): Hey everyone, thanks for joining—quick intros, then we want to scope the POC for capacity and autoscale.
00:18 - Dr. Priya: Thanks Lila, we want to make sure the prototype handles our clinical report generation traffic, which is spiky, especially 7–10am PST when clinicians bulk generate reports. We're concerned about p95 latency under peak and cost.
00:35 - Marco: Got it. Can you give ballpark traffic numbers for peak and baseline?
00:48 - Samir: Baseline is about 8 requests/sec across the cluster, but peak bursts hit ~110 requests/sec sustained for 3–7 minutes, and occasional back-to-back bursts during shift change. TTL on requests is tight; product needs p95 < 250ms for single-turn summarization otherwise clinicians complain.
01:08 - Marco: OK, that's helpful. Are most requests short sequences? Token lengths?
01:20 - Eric: Average prompt + completion ~180 tokens, but some go to 800 tokens for long case summaries. Distribution is heavy-tailed. We can provide traces.
01:35 - Jin: That variability matters a lot for batching and KV caching. If you get many short requests we can optimize for lower latency with smaller batch windows; long ones push GPU memory and KV cache hit behavior.
01:51 - Lila: One of our POC patterns is reserved capacity with a burst pool—reserved GPUs handle baseline and steady load, burst capacity kicks in for short spikes. When burst is exhausted we can fall back to a quantized model or route to a regional queue. We should talk tradeoffs.
02:08 - Meghan: What's the typical granularity for reserved pools? Do you recommend one node or a pool of several?
02:18 - Marco: We size reserved by baseline QPS and target utilization. For your baseline 8 req/s and p95 250ms, with model M-3 (a 16GB variant) we estimate needing 2x reserved instances to handle baseline comfortably at 60–70% utilization. Then configure burst up to 6 additional GPUs for short spikes. But we want to run a real benchmark against your prompts.
02:42 - Dr. Priya: We prefer predictable cost. Will reserved + burst still let us cap spend?
02:48 - Lila: Yes—reserved is committed and predictable, burst is metered; we can set a burst budget and automatic fallback when budget exhausted. For POC we usually recommend a simulated 4-week spend model so you can see actual numbers.
03:06 - Samir: What happens when burst and reserved are saturated? We need graceful degradation not hard failures.
03:12 - Jin: Options: 1) Route to a smaller, quantized model (e.g., M-3-8q) that runs on cheaper instances and gives slightly lower quality but 2–3x lower latency cost; 2) Serve from prefix caches for repeated queries; 3) Queue requests with client-side retry/backoff and progress indicators. For clinician UX we prefer model fallbacks + cached responses rather than visible errors.
03:40 - Meghan: Any impact on tokens and billing when falling back?
03:46 - Marco: The token billing depends on model variant; quantized smaller model still counts tokens but at different cost per token. We'll include that in the cost worksheet.
03:55 - Lila: Let's capture success criteria for the POC. What does Apollo consider "win"?
04:02 - Dr. Priya: Three things: (1) p95 latency < 250ms for 95% of daytime traffic; (2) cost per 10k report < $X (we'll give target later); (3) no user-visible errors during simulated bursts (use fallback instead).
04:18 - Lila: Noted. We'll make the benchmark measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, model quality (BLEU/ROUGE-ish automated checks vs gold summaries), and percent of fallbacks used.
04:33 - Eric: For automated quality we need output equivalence checks; if we fallback we want a quality delta threshold.
04:41 - Jin: We'll add an eval threshold: fallback model must have >90% similarity by your metrics or else we prefer queuing + user warning.
04:51 - Samir: Region/residency is a constraint. Some patient data must stay in us-west-2—can burst cross region?
05:00 - Marco: For POC we can keep everything in us-west-2. Redwood Private or Dedicated can be pinned to region; hosted burst can be configured similarly. There is slightly higher latency for cross-region fallbacks, that's why we prefer local quantized fallbacks.
05:16 - Meghan: OK, timeline — we talked about 4-week POC earlier, does that still stand?
05:22 - Lila: Yes, recommended POC timeline: Week 0 (prep + dataset and tracing), Week 1 (baseline deploy + initial benchmark), Week 2 (tuning autoscale and cache), Week 3 (stress bursts + fallback tuning), Week 4 (report & handover). We can compress if you want but prefer full 4 weeks for meaningful cost numbers.
05:38 - Dr. Priya: Week 0 we can provide traces and sample prompts; when do you need them?
05:44 - Lila: ASAP—by next Monday would be ideal. We'll start with a 100k-token benchmark set and expand.
05:53 - Marco: For benchmarking we'll use two payload mixes: 80% short (<=200 tokens) and 20% long (>400 tokens). We'll measure under synthetic diurnal pattern and measured burst pattern from your traces.
06:08 - Eric: For long stories, do you recommend different model variants?
06:12 - Jin: Sometimes you run the long jobs on a separate pool to avoid blocking short latency requests; or allocate exclusive slots for long requests. Another pattern is preemptible long pool with lower priority.
06:26 - Samir: Can Redwood give a template autoscale policy? We'd like defaults we can tweak.
06:31 - Marco: Yes, we'll share a policy template: min_replicas, target_utilization, max_replicas, burst_bucket_size, warm_pool_size, fallback_order. Example: min 2, target_util 60%, max 8, warm-pool 2 for sub-second cold starts. We'll include numbers tuned to your profiles after the first benchmark.
06:56 - Lila: About warm pools — cold model loads are expensive and slow. For quantized 8-bit models the cold start is faster but can still be a few seconds. Warm pool ensures immediate capacity for common models, we typically recommend a small warm pool tailored to your most frequent model variant.
07:14 - Meghan: In failure scenarios do we want regional fallback or model fallback first?
07:18 - Jin: Model fallback first (local quantized) because it keeps data local; regional fallback is last resort due to cross-region latency and data residency.
07:28 - Dr. Priya: Security questions — we will need SOC2 docs, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs. How does that work for POC?
07:36 - Lila: We'll share our SOC2 summary and security playbook. For KMS we can integrate with your key management for Private deployments; for hosted POC we can offer customer-managed keys for specific setups. Audit logs are available in the console and can be exported. We'll attach relevant docs.
07:52 - Samir: Ok good. Regarding quotas and throttles, can we set hard caps so our upstream can't overwhelm the system?
07:58 - Marco: Yes, per-route quotas, token rate limits, and backpressure signals can be configured. We'll default to soft throttles for POC and recommend production hard caps later.
08:10 - Meghan: Benchmark success thresholds again? p95 < 250ms daytime, <400ms during burst with fallbacks, and fallback rate < 10% ideally?
08:20 - Lila: We'll agree on those and record them in the POC charter. If fallback rate exceeds 10% we'll iterate on reserved sizing or warm pool.
08:28 - Eric: What test harness do you use? Would you accept a k6 or Locust workload?
08:33 - Marco: We can accept k6/Locust traces. Our SEs prefer the harness that can replay your exact traces; we can also provide a lightweight runner.
08:45 - Dr. Priya: Any caveats about tokenization differences between our local tokenizer and the models?
08:49 - Jin: Yes, slight tokenization variation can change token counts. We'll run the tokenization pass with your prompts during setup to ensure accurate cost estimates.
09:00 - Lila: Ok, responsibilities: Apollo to share traces and quality metric, Redwood to run the baseline benchmark and sizing recommendation.
09:08 - Meghan: Who runs the initial bench? Redwood or Apollo?
09:12 - Marco: Redwood SE will run the initial bench in partnership with Apollo infra — we need access to the sample data and a test API key or a staging hook.
09:24 - Dr. Priya: We need an NDA addendum for HIPAA-ish compliance — is that possible for POC?
09:29 - Lila: Yes we have a PII/HIPAA addendum we can attach. We'll loop legal.
09:36 - Eric: A quick nit: for long-running bursts are there preemption policies? If a long job runs and a burst hits, what happens?
09:42 - Jin: Preemption policy can evict long, low-priority jobs or pause them and resume later. We'll show configurations: preempt vs isolate.
09:50 - Meghan: Will you provide a graphic or runbook for the fallback sequence? That helps our product team.
09:55 - Lila: Yes, we'll deliver a short playbook: triggers -> fallback order -> operator alerts -> rollback plan.
10:04 - Samir: Cost question — can you provide an example cost per 10k reports for reserved+burst vs fully hosted?
10:11 - Lila: We'll include sample numbers in the spreadsheet; general guidance: reserved lowers per-unit compute cost but requires commit; burst is higher per-unit but reduces commit. For your workload we expect reserved-first to be cheaper if you're above X reports/day — we'll compute that with your traces.
10:30 - Marco: For the benchmark we'll measure: 1) p50/p95/p99 across prompt distribution, 2) tokens consumed, 3) fallback counts and quality metrics, 4) cost delta for each fallback type, 5) regional latency if we test cross-region.
10:47 - Dr. Priya: Who do we loop in for infra deep-dive? Samir, Eric and our SRE lead; schedule next week.
10:55 - Lila: I'll send a Calendly for a 90-minute deep technical session and attach the POC charter draft.
11:02 - Meghan: Any recommended warm-pool sizes for our profile?
11:05 - Marco: Start with warm-pool 2 for the primary model and adjust post-benchmark. Warm pools are measured in GPUs or model instances depending on runtime.
11:14 - Jin: One more note on batch windows—very small windows reduce throughput but improve latency, we'll tune that in Week 2. For the POC we'll test two window strategies: 10ms and 40ms.
11:29 - Eric: Do you support model pinning and version rollbacks in the POC? We might need to test a rollback mid-stress.
11:34 - Marco: Yes, rollouts and automatic rollback based on error/quality triggers are supported. We'll demonstrate canary and automatic fallback.
11:44 - Lila: Recap and confirm next steps: Redwood runs initial 100k-token benchmark using Apollo traces, we share pricing, Apollo provides traces and gold-label quality sets, schedule deep-dive next week, legal addendum for PII.
11:58 - Dr. Priya: That sounds good, thanks everyone.
12:02 - Lila: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the deck and the worksheets.
12:08 - (recording ends)

NOTES / ARTIFACT LINKS: "POC Charter (draft)" (link in chat), "Reserved+Burst cost worksheet" (to be shared), security playbook PDF (will be shared), sample harness repo (github link).

TRANSCRIPTION NOTES: few words mis-heard by auto transcript (e.g., "KV cache" appears as "K-V cash" in some spots), speaker overlap occasionally attributed to Speaker 3.
